A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have designed a distributed, tiled, dynamic execution microarchitecture that supports the full instruction set of a 64 bit RISC-V ISA, and we have implemented the microarchitecture in the TRIPS prototype processor.

we have demonstrated that it is possible to build a distributed microarchitecture that supports a large number of threads, a large on-chip memory, and a large number of instructions per cycle, while providing the same performance as a centralized microarchitecture.
TRIPS is a distributed, tiled architecture with distributed microarchitectures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the control and communication protocols for distributed microarchitectures are not fundamentally different from those in centralized designs.

distributed microarchitectures can be designed and implemented with a high degree of control and data locality, and that the resulting performance and power characteristics of the design are competitive with centralized microarchitectures.
distributed microarchitectures can be implemented in a straightforward manner by using a small set of distributed protocols that are similar to those in centralized designs.
